She usually ______ a letter to her friend once a week.
questions.explanation: In the Simple Present, third-person singular subjects (she/he/it) add -s to the verb (writes) for routine actions indicated by 'usually'.

questions.q: He ______ at the gym every morning.
questions.explanation: 'Every morning' signals a habitual routine. 'He' takes the third-person singular verb ending -s (exercises).

questions.q: Water ______ at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: General scientific facts use the Simple Present. 'Water' is an uncountable (singular) noun, requiring boils.

questions.q: He ______ in Sana'a.
questions.explanation: Permanent situations use the Simple Present tense with third-person singular -s (lives).

questions.q: The sun ______ in the east.
questions.explanation: General facts about nature require the Simple Present singular verb form (rises).

questions.q: She ______ football on weekdays.
questions.explanation: Negative Simple Present sentences for 'she' use does not followed by the base verb (play).

questions.q: They ______ dinner together as a family each night when they are busy.
questions.explanation: Plural subjects ('they') use do not + base verb (eat) in Simple Present negative forms.

questions.q: ______ she write a letter every Monday?
questions.explanation: Yes/No questions in the Present Simple with 'she' start with the auxiliary verb Does.

questions.q: ______ he play football once a week?
questions.explanation: Habitual question forms with 'he' require auxiliary Does.

questions.q: Where ______ they work?
questions.explanation: WH-questions for present routines with plural subject 'they' use auxiliary do (Where do they work?).

questions.q: What time ______ he usually exercise every morning?
questions.explanation: WH-question auxiliary for singular 'he' in present routine is does.

questions.q: They ______ eat dinner together as a family each night.
questions.explanation: Usually is an adverb of frequency used between the subject and verb in Simple Present.

questions.q: She ______ Mekkah last summer.
questions.explanation: 'Last summer' specifies a completed past action. Regular verbs form the past tense by adding -ed (visited).

questions.q: We ______ our project two days ago.
questions.explanation: 'Two days ago' requires the regular past tense form finished.

questions.q: They ______ at 3 p.m. yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Meet' is an irregular verb. Its Simple Past (V2) form for completed actions yesterday is met.

questions.q: She ______ a letter yesterday afternoon.
questions.explanation: 'Write' is irregular. The past tense V2 form for a completed action yesterday is wrote.

questions.q: He ______ football yesterday.
questions.explanation: Simple Past negative forms use did not + base verb (play), never the double past form.

questions.q: She ______ write a letter last night.
questions.explanation: Negative completed past actions require auxiliary did not followed by base verb (write).

questions.q: ______ she write a letter yesterday?
questions.explanation: Yes/No questions for past events use auxiliary Did.

questions.q: ______ he play football during the match last Sunday?
questions.explanation: 'Last Sunday' requires auxiliary Did for past question formation.

questions.q: What time ______ she call you this morning?
questions.explanation: WH-question auxiliary for a specific completed past time is did.

questions.q: Where ______ they meet at 3 p.m. yesterday?
questions.explanation: Past event WH-questions use auxiliary did + subject + base verb.

questions.q: Yesterday, my father ______ tea instead of coffee.
questions.explanation: 'Drink' is an irregular verb. The past V2 form for yesterday's action is drank.

questions.q: He usually walks to work, but yesterday he ______ the bus.
questions.explanation: Contrasting present habit with past event: 'take' becomes irregular past took.

questions.q: They ______ their grandparents every summer, but last year they ______ to the beach instead.
questions.explanation: 'Every summer' takes Present Simple (visit), while 'last year' takes Past Simple irregular (went).

questions.q: Yemen is located in the northern part of the Arabian Peninsula.
Yemen had no role in trading items like frankincense, myrrh, and spices.
In 1990, Yemen unified after being divided into North and South Yemen.
Yemen's location at the entrance to the Red Sea is important for global shipping.
Yemen's strategic importance has decreased over time.
Choose the closest meaning to: Strategic
Choose the closest meaning to: Trade
Choose the closest meaning to: Control
Choose the closest meaning to: Peninsula
options: A land with water on all sides
A land with water on most sides

questions.q: Choose the closest meaning to: Wealth
Choose the closest meaning to: Key
Choose the closest meaning to: Role
Choose the closest meaning to: Unified
Choose the closest meaning to: Heritage
Choose the closest meaning to: Significant
Vocabulary - Closest meaning to: Artificial
questions.explanation: Artificial means man-made rather than natural.

questions.q: Vocabulary - Closest meaning to: Advanced
questions.explanation: Advanced means highly developed.

questions.q: Vocabulary - Closest meaning to: Tasks
questions.explanation: Tasks refers to duties or work to be done.

questions.q: Vocabulary - Closest meaning to: Recognize
questions.explanation: Recognize means to identify something previously known or encountered.

questions.q: Vocabulary - Closest meaning to: Speech
questions.explanation: Speech refers to talking or spoken language.

questions.q: Vocabulary - Closest meaning to: Program
questions.explanation: A program is a set of instructions written for a computer.

questions.q: Vocabulary - Closest meaning to: Adapt
questions.explanation: Adapt means to adjust to new conditions.

questions.q: Vocabulary - Closest meaning to: Data
questions.explanation: Data refers to information such as numbers and facts.

questions.q: Vocabulary - Closest meaning to: Understand
questions.explanation: Understand means to comprehend or know the meaning.

questions.q: Vocabulary - Closest meaning to: Capable
questions.explanation: Capable means able to do something.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly follows the affirmative form Subject + will + base verb?
options: She will helps me with my project.
She'll help me with my project.
She will helping me with my project.
She'll to help me with my project.
questions.explanation: Will is followed directly by the base verb (help) without -s, -ing, or to.

questions.q: What is the correct negative sentence structure for will?
questions.explanation: The negative structure is Subject + will not (won't) + base verb.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct question form using will?
questions.explanation: Questions with will invert the subject and auxiliary: Will + subject + base verb?

questions.q: Select the correct short affirmative answer to: "Will she call me?"
questions.explanation: The short affirmative answer pattern is Yes, [subject] + will.

questions.q: Choose the correct negative short answer for: "Will they stay here?"
questions.explanation: The short negative answer pattern is No, [subject] + won't.

questions.q: Speaker A: "Oh, it's raining!" / Speaker B: "I ______ an umbrella then." (Instant decision)
questions.explanation: Spontaneous decisions made at the moment of speaking take will + base verb.

questions.q: Speaker A: "The door is unlocked." / Speaker B: "I ______ it right now."
questions.explanation: An instant reaction to new information uses will lock.

questions.q: Speaker A: "The room is dirty." / Speaker B: "I ______ it."
questions.explanation: Deciding to clean upon noticing the situation uses will clean.

questions.q: Why do we use will in: "A: I'm hungry. B: I'll make a sandwich."?
options: To describe a fixed plan made days ago.
To express a decision made at the moment of speaking.
questions.explanation: Responding immediately to someone's hunger is an instant decision made while speaking.

questions.q: Which of the following expressions is commonly used with will to signal a prediction?
questions.explanation: Phrases like I think, probably, maybe, and I'm sure introduce predictions with will.

questions.q: Complete the prediction: "I think our team ______ the match."
questions.explanation: Predictions following I think use will + base verb.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct negative form: "He probably ______ come to the party."
questions.explanation: Negative predictions with adverbs like probably use won't + base verb.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly represents a prediction using maybe?
questions.explanation: Predictions with maybe take will + base verb.

questions.q: Select the prediction expressing certainty (I'm sure):
options: I'm sure she will pass the exam.
She is passing the exam right now.
I'm sure she to pass the exam.
questions.explanation: Expressing prediction certainty takes I'm sure + subject + will + base verb.

questions.q: Which sentence expresses a promise?
options: I am meeting Saleh at 3:00 p.m.
Are you having dinner with us?
We are flying to Paris next Monday.
questions.explanation: Commitments to future behavior express a promise.

questions.q: "Don't worry, I won't tell anyone your secret." This sentence is an example of a:
questions.explanation: Promising confidentiality with won't is a promise.

questions.q: Speaker A: "The bag looks heavy." / Speaker B: "I'll ______ it for you." (Offer)
questions.explanation: Offers use I'll + base verb (carry).

questions.q: Speaker A: "I don't have a ride." / Speaker B: "I'll ______ you home."
questions.explanation: Offering help uses I'll + base verb (drive).

questions.q: Speaker A: "I'm thirsty." / Speaker B: "______ get you a glass of water."
questions.explanation: Offering assistance spontaneously uses I'll.

questions.q: When do we use the Present Continuous (am/is/are + verb-ing) for the future?
options: For instant decisions made while talking.
For fixed future plans or arrangements (with specific person, time, or place).
For general predictions with I think.
questions.explanation: Present Continuous is used for fixed arrangements already planned with specific details.

questions.q: "We ______ to Paris next Monday. Our tickets are already booked." Which form shows a fixed arrangement?
questions.explanation: Already booked tickets signal a fixed arrangement, taking are flying.

questions.q: "I ______ Saleh at the airport at 3:00 p.m. tomorrow." Choose the correct fixed plan form:
questions.explanation: A planned meeting at a set time and location requires Present Continuous (am meeting).

questions.q: Which negative sentence correctly expresses a fixed plan for this evening?
options: He won't coming to the party this evening.
He isn't coming to the party this evening.
He not coming to the party this evening.
He isn't come to the party this evening.
questions.explanation: Negative fixed arrangement structure: Subject + am/is/are + not + verb-ing.

questions.q: Select the correct question form for a fixed future arrangement tonight:
questions.explanation: Arrangement questions use Am/Is/Are + subject + verb-ing?

questions.q: Which sentence describes a spontaneous decision rather than a fixed plan?
options: I am meeting my doctor at 10:00 a.m. tomorrow.
The room is dirty. I will clean it.
We are flying to London next week.
questions.explanation: Deciding to clean upon seeing a dirty room is a spontaneous decision (will clean).

questions.q: A: I'm thirsty. B: I ______ you some water. (get)
questions.explanation: Instant offer/decision at the moment of speaking uses will get.

questions.q: I ______ Sarah at 6:00 tomorrow. (meet)
questions.explanation: A scheduled meeting at a specific time tomorrow uses Present Continuous (am meeting).

questions.q: They ______ a new house next year. They have already made the plans. (buy)
questions.explanation: Already made plans point to a fixed arrangement using are buying.

questions.q: I think our team ______ the game. (win)
questions.explanation: Predictions with I think use will win.

questions.q: We ______ to Aden next weekend. We already have our tickets. (travel)
questions.explanation: Already having tickets indicates a fixed arrangement: are traveling.

questions.q: Don't worry. I ______ you. (help)
questions.explanation: Reassuring someone with a promise/offer uses will help.

questions.q: She ______ dinner with her parents tonight. (have)
questions.explanation: A fixed evening arrangement with family uses Present Continuous (is having).

questions.q: Maybe it ______ tomorrow. (rain)
questions.explanation: Predictions introduced by maybe use will rain.

questions.q: The doorbell is ringing. I ______ the door. (open)
questions.explanation: Reacting immediately to the doorbell uses will open.

questions.q: Look at those dark clouds! It ______ soon. (rain)
questions.explanation: Future prediction uses will rain.

questions.q: These bags are very heavy. I ______ you.
questions.explanation: Offering immediate help uses will help.

questions.q: You need a pen. Here you are. I ______ you mine.
questions.explanation: Offering a pen on the spot uses will give.

questions.q: A: Where are you going tomorrow? B: I ______ my friend at the café at 5 p.m.
questions.explanation: A planned meeting at a specific time and place uses am meeting.

questions.q: A: What are you doing tonight? B: I ______ dinner at my friend's house.
questions.explanation: A fixed arrangement for tonight uses Present Continuous (am having).

questions.q: Sarah studies very hard. I think she ______ the exam.
questions.explanation: A prediction following I think uses will pass.

questions.q: A: Are you free tonight? B: No. I ______ dinner with my parents.
questions.explanation: Having a fixed arrangement tonight takes am having.

questions.q: A: Do you think John will like the present? B: Yes, I'm sure he ______ it.
questions.explanation: Predictions with I'm sure use will like.

questions.q: A: Are you going to the party tonight? B: Yes. I ______ there with Ahmed.
questions.explanation: An existing plan/arrangement to go with someone uses am going.

questions.q: A: Please be careful with my laptop. B: Don't worry. I ______ careful.
questions.explanation: Making a promise/assurance for the future uses will be.

questions.q: A: I can't open this bottle. B: Give it to me. I ______ it.
questions.explanation: Volunteering immediately to open it uses will open.

questions.q: Error recognition - Which sentence is correct?
options: I am meet my friend tonight.
I am meeting my friend tonight.
I will meeting my friend tonight.
questions.explanation: Present Continuous requires am/is/are + verb-ing: I am meeting my friend tonight.

questions.q: Error recognition - Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Correct question structure: Will + subject + base verb.

questions.q: Error recognition - Which sentence is correct?
options: I will helps you with your homework.
I'll helping you with your homework.
I'll to help you with your homework.
I'll help you with your homework.
questions.explanation: After 'll (will), use the base verb without -s, -ing, or to.

questions.q: Error recognition - Which sentence is correct?
options: We traveling to Aden next week.
We are travel to Aden next week.
We are traveling to Aden next week.
We are will travel to Aden next week.
questions.explanation: Correct Present Continuous form: are + traveling.
